hypotheses: A covering {U_i→U} of a site C, sheaves F,G, and compatible maps between their restrictions to each C/U_i.
conclusions: There is a unique morphism F|_{C/U}→G|_{C/U} whose restriction agrees with each local morphism.

hypotheses: Three sheaves F,G,H on a site C.
conclusions: Natural adjunction Hom(F×G,H)≅Hom(F,SheafHom(G,H)).

hypotheses: A site C, object U, and sheaf F.
conclusions: SheafHom(h_U#,F) is canonically isomorphic to j_{U*}(F restricted to C/U).

hypotheses: A site C, a covering {U_i→U}, and a family of sheaves with descent isomorphisms φ_ij satisfying the standard cocycle law.
conclusions: There exists a sheaf F on C/U with isomorphisms to the local F_i respecting all overlap maps.

hypotheses: A site C and a covering {U_i→U}.
conclusions: The category of sheaves on C/U is equivalent to the category of gluing data associated to this covering.

hypotheses: A site C.
conclusions: The category Sh(C) is equivalent to the source-defined category of absolute gluing data.
lemma-glue-sheaves-absolute.hold_reason: Absolute gluing data require their source definition from the section, not a generic Čech family.

hypotheses: A subcanonical site C, an object U, and a sheaf G on C/U.
conclusions: The extension j_{U!}G is already given without sheafification by the coproduct of G(V→U) over maps V→U.

hypotheses: A site C having products of pairs of objects and an object U.
conclusions: j_U has a continuous right adjoint v(X)=X×U/U.
v defines a morphism of sites whose topos morphism equals j_U.
j_{U*}F(X)=F(X×U/U).

hypotheses: A site C with fibre products and an arrow U→V.
conclusions: The induced j:C/U→C/V has continuous right adjoint v(X/V)=X×_V U/U.
v defines a morphism of sites with topos morphism j.
j_*F(X/V)=F(X×_V U/U).

hypotheses: A site C, an object U such that every object has at most one arrow to U, and a sheaf F on C/U.
conclusions: Both canonical maps F→j_U^-1 j_{U!}F and j_U^-1j_{U*}F→F are isomorphisms.

hypotheses: A site C and a commutative square of objects U',U,V',V.
conclusions: The induced localization functors and their topoi morphisms form two commutative squares.
If the original square is Cartesian, the stated base-change identity for inverse image and direct image holds.

hypotheses: A morphism of sites f:C→D induced by continuous u:D→C, and V∈Ob(D), U=u(V).
conclusions: The induced u':D/V→C/U gives a site morphism f':C/U→D/V and a commutative diagram of topoi.
Under the corresponding slice-topos equivalences, (f')^-1 acts by pulling back the map to h_V#.
The pushforward and restriction functors satisfy f'_* j_U^-1=j_V^-1 f_*.

hypotheses: A cocontinuous functor u:C→D between sites, and U∈C with V=u(U).
conclusions: The induced u':C/U→D/V is cocontinuous and yields a commuting diagram of localized sites and topoi.

hypotheses: A cocontinuous u:C→D, object V of D, and source-defined right-indexing category of pairs (U,ψ:u(U)→V).
conclusions: The right-indexing category becomes a site using underlying C-coverings.
The projection to C is continuous and cocontinuous; the projection to D/V is cocontinuous.
These functors give a commuting square of topoi and f'_*j^-1=j_V^-1 f_*.

hypotheses: A commuting square of four cocontinuous functors between sites, with both horizontal functors also continuous and a stated cofinality condition on right-indexing categories.
conclusions: The specified comparison identities f'_*∘(g')^-1=g^-1∘f_* and g'_!∘(f')^-1=f^-1∘g_! hold.

hypotheses: A continuous and cocontinuous u:C→D satisfying local faithfulness, local fullness, and local essential surjectivity on object coverings as in the five enumerated conditions.
conclusions: Its associated morphism of topoi Sh(C)→Sh(D) is an equivalence.

hypotheses: A special cocontinuous u:C→D and an object U in C.
conclusions: The induced C/U→D/u(U) is also special cocontinuous, hence induces an equivalence of localized topoi.

hypotheses: A site C and a set-sized full subcategory C'⊂Sh(C) containing each h_U# and stable under fibre products; declare jointly epimorphic families as coverings.
conclusions: After choosing a set of equivalent covering families C' is a site.
The topology of C' is subcanonical.
U↦h_U# is special cocontinuous and yields an equivalence of topoi.
For F∈C', g^-1h_F=F.
For U∈C, g_*h_U#=h_{h_U#}.

hypotheses: A topos Sh(C) and a set of its sheaves {F_i}.
conclusions: There exists an equivalent site C' satisfying subcanonicality, canonical-covering characterization, finite limits, representability of subsheaves of representables, and representability of the images of every F_i.

hypotheses: A morphism f:Sh(C)→Sh(D) of topoi.
conclusions: There exists a site C', special cocontinuous v:C→C', and continuous fibre-product-preserving u:D→C' defining a morphism of sites, such that f factors as the associated equivalence of topoi followed by that site-induced morphism.

hypotheses: A site C and sheaf F, with the category C/F of pairs (U,s∈F(U)) and coverings defined by those in C.
conclusions: The forgetful j:C/F→C is continuous and cocontinuous, induces a topos morphism and equivalence Sh(C/F)≃Sh(C)/F identifying j with the slice localization.

hypotheses: A site C, object U, and F=h_U#.
conclusions: The slice localization j_F:Sh(C)/F→Sh(C) is the localized site morphism j_U:Sh(C/U)→Sh(C) under the standard equivalence Sh(C/U)≃Sh(C)/h_U#.

hypotheses: A site C and a map s:G→F of sheaves.
conclusions: There is a natural commutative localization triangle of topoi Sh(C)/G→Sh(C)/F→Sh(C).
Its left inverse image is H/F↦(H×_F G→G).
Its left adjoint extension sends (E→G) to (E→G→F).

hypotheses: A site C, arrow V→U, and induced map of associated representable sheaves h_V#→h_U#.
conclusions: The localization triangle of slice topoi for h_V#→h_U# agrees with the site-localization triangle C/V→C/U→C under both standard slice identifications.
